entries.title: Job 21:2
segments: Let this be your consolations; if you will candidly listen to me, I will accept this in place of the consolations I might have so reasonably expected of you.

entries.title: Job 21:4
segments:
Is my complaint to man? merely, or principally. 
 
  And if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled? better, omitting the italics, which are not in the original, to read, "And why should not my spirit be troubled?" that is, in view of the mighty afflictions laid upon me by God's hand. 
 
In our trials and distresses we should look not so much to men for help, as to God; and feel that whoever or whatever may be the instrument, he is the only source of relief.

entries.title: Job 21:5
segments:
Mark me; behold my affliction. 
 
  Lay your hand upon your mouth; be silent.

entries.title: Job 21:7
segments: The wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty; this, in opposition to the doctrine of Job's friends, is often the case.

The wicked are sometimes prospered in this world, and receive more outward blessings than their pious neighbors.  They may live longer, and die in less distress.  The reason of this is to men not known, and it sometimes occasions them great perplexity.

entries.title: Job 21:13
segments: In a moment; without long, lingering illness.

entries.title: Job 21:16
segments: Not in their hand; not in their own power.  It comes from God, and they are wholly dependent on him.

entries.title: Job 21:17
segments: How oft; many understand this question as extending to the following verses

, which may then be read interrogatively thus: How oft doth God distribute?  how oft are they as stubble? etc.; and as meaning to affirm that such a thing seldom happens, or rather, does not happen to the wicked more than to the righteous.  But see note to

. 
 
However prosperous may be the condition of the wicked in this world, or however adverse that of the righteous, in the future world it will be reversed; the righteous will be comforted, and the wicked tormented.

entries.title: Job 21:21
segments: What pleasure hath he in his house after him; when the wicked man's days are ended, he can have no more interest in the lot of his children.  If they be cut off, that does not affect him.

entries.title: Job 21:26
segments: They shall lie down alike; God does not deal with them here according to their character, but treats them in many respects alike.

entries.title: Job 21:28
segments: Where is the house of the prince? meaning, of me, Job, who once lived as a prince.

entries.title: Job 21:29
segments:
Them that go by the way? travellers, who have had the opportunity of extended observation. 
 
  Their tokens; the indications which they give of the course of God's providence.

entries.title: Job 21:30
segments:
Is reserved to the day of destruction; now he is suffered to prosper, being reserved for destruction hereafter. 
 
The fact that men are not treated according to their character in this world, is evidence of a coming judgment, when a just discrimination will be made, and each one receive according to his works.

entries.title: Job 21:31
segments: Who shall repay him; no one in this world; but God shall reward him in the world to come.

entries.title: Job 21:32
segments: And shall remain in the tomb; literally, and shall watch over the mound, meaning the sepulchral mound.  Some render this clause impersonally: "and one shall watch over the mound;" that is, the sepulchral mound of this powerful and prosperous sinner shall be carefully guarded.  Others understand it as a poetical descrition, by which he is represented as watching, through his monumental inscription, over his grave.

entries.title: Job 21:33
segments: Every man; shall in like manner go to the grave.
